scope.implemented: A development-only fixed-context authorization declaration and obligation compiler with numbered source catalogs, narrow wire v1, host-bound canonical citations, provider-bound deadlines and lifecycle events, compact repair, layered semantic/transport/delivery evaluation, resumable comparison runner, and read-only V replay.
scope.evaluated: Three existing Open WebUI development cases, each as one matched organized-instruction B and authorization-domain-method D pair at one fixed repository/ref and one model route.
excluded: production CLI or default product integration
target project execution or live deployment probing
held-out, cross-project, or general-security effectiveness claims
a second representation or a second project

legacyTaskDecisionCorrect.note: The v0 field counts the two valid unknown dispositions as false; semanticDecisionCorrect is the W method field.

DMinusB.interpretation: Descriptive small-panel operational difference only; no semantic-quality advantage was observed.

revision.reason: The six real units left only semantic relation omissions shared across the trusted-header answers, so no provider revision, answer hint, or rubric relaxation was justified. A later W9 code review found a separate invalid-wire canonical-result leakage path; it was fixed with deterministic red-green tests and did not require rerunning six already-valid final artifacts.

independentBorderlineReview.scope: The two trusted-header final answers against the fixed v1 rubric.
agreements: Both unknown dispositions and both bounded scope claims are supported.
D omits the optional signup path.
Both answers omit an explicit enumeration of all four conditional outcomes.
disputed: The independent reviewer counted B's password gate and optional signup as supported because the bound citation quote contains the relevant code. The final development review applied the stricter rubric wording that the answer must state those relations, so it recorded them as missing.
independentBorderlineReview.adjudication: Use the stricter explicit-statement interpretation; preserve the disagreement rather than changing the answer, rubric, or score to make a method look better.

methodFeasibility.recommendedScope: Keep the shared declaration, narrow transport, host citation binding, lifecycle accounting, and layered evaluator for fixed-context development studies. Do not promote B or D to a production default, general security DSL, cross-project method, or active-discovery system.
methodFeasibility.methodDecision: D is an operationally promising experiment arm, not a demonstrated quality winner. Preserve B as the simpler matched baseline and retain the common domain model while studying the missing relations.
evidence: All six results were transport-valid, delivery-complete, and semantically correct at the disposition level.
D used fewer provider calls and tokens in this three-pair run.
D did not improve critical-fact support: both trusted-header answers were partial.
The remaining omissions concern conditional outcomes and identity provisioning, not mechanical result transport.

unresolvedIssues: How to represent control state, authentication outcomes, identity provisioning, deployment boundaries, and protected effects without encoding case answers.
Whether D's lower call and token use repeats across new runs, routes, or projects; this run is too small for a general efficiency claim.
Whether an explicit generic relation representation improves evidence completeness without increasing prompt burden or overclaiming deployment facts.
Actual USD was unavailable for every W provider call.

minimumImplementation: Add or prototype one generic relation layer for control state, authentication outcome, identity provisioning, deployment boundary, and protected effect; do not add case names or expected answers.
Keep wire v1, host-bound citations, shared B/D facts, zero executable tools, and the existing three-case development panel unchanged.
Measure whether the trusted-header optional signup and four conditional outcomes become explicitly supported while file/text do not regress; do not start a second project first.
successCriteria: The new relation layer is task-generic and compiles from the same canonical facts for both arms.
Strict post-generation review supports the previously missing trusted-header relations without answer hints or rubric changes.
Transport, delivery, lifecycle accounting, and the two already-full cases remain valid.

independentCodeReview.finding: Invalid obligation or uninformative-unknown diagnostics could coexist with a canonical result and be delivered by the host.
independentCodeReview.resolution: Added failing normalizer and host tests, then made every error-level normalization diagnostic suppress the canonical result; focused 17/17 and the full 77/77 authorization suite passed. No additional findings were reported.
